dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), developed by NaCl for Japan Medical Association. Compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL/CICS, uses INDEXED files with DYNAMIC access.
evidence: SELECT ... ASSIGN ... ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC
no COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
49 COPY statements typical of GnuCOBOL ORCA codebase

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system - specifically point-score aggregation for hospitalization (入院) claims including nursing care and self-pay categories
purpose.summary: ORCR0840 is a large batch program in the JMA ORCA medical receipt software suite. It processes and aggregates diagnosis/treatment point scores by category for inpatient (hospitalization) medical insurance claims. The program handles complex Japanese medical billing rules including nursing care fees, self-pay calculations, and various special treatment codes across many revision cycles from 2003 to 2013.

notable_features: 49 COPY statements indicating heavy use of shared copybooks
550 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
INDEXED files with DYNAMIC access mode (ISAM-style)
No COMP-3 packed decimal (uses standard numeric PIC)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Long revision history spanning 2003-2013 with named developers (NACL team)
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments contain Japanese text encoded in EUC-JP (multibyte characters appear as latin-1 sequences). This is the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system, well-known in Japanese healthcare IT. The program name ORCR0840 follows the ORCA naming convention. Source is fixed-format COBOL with lines up to 80 characters (57 lines exceed column 72, likely due to long data names or comments).
